findings.source_passage: worse than an Assyrian city in the plague, when the living are incompetent to bury the departed. So intolerable indeed is it regarded by some, that no cupidity could persuade them
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4, description of the blasted whale's odor
findings.why_it_matters: The 'Assyrian city in the plague' simile and the 'no cupidity could persuade them' clause are rhetorically distinctive — they carry Melville's characteristic elevation of a comic-grotesque situation into grand historical register. The draft reduces this to 'worse than a plague city.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'worse than an Assyrian city in the plague, when the living are incompetent to bury the departed' and the sentence about cupidity; these are voice-establishing amplifications that define the chapter's rhetorical tone.

findings.source_passage: wouldn't be fit to burn in a jail; no, not in a condemned cell. And as for the other whale, why, I'll agree to get more oil by chopping up and trying out these three masts of ours
findings.source_locator: Stubb's long speech in the bows, paragraph 6
findings.why_it_matters: Stubb's extended mock-charitable speech ('pass round a hat,' 'not fit to burn in a jail,' 'chopping up these three masts') is a signature comic set-piece that establishes his voice and the ambergris foreshadowing; the draft collapses it to a few phrases and loses both the comedic rhythm and the jail/condemned-cell jab.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the jail/condemned-cell line and the masts-for-oil hyperbole; these are the punch lines of Stubb's speech and the voice-establishing heart of the passage.

findings.source_passage: the whole terminating in a symmetrical folded bulb of a bright red colour. Upon her head boards, in large gilt letters, he read "Bouton de Rose,"—Rose-button, or Rose-bud; and this was the romantic name of this aromatic ship.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'the romantic name of this aromatic ship' is a small but perfect Melvillean pun-and-irony closing flourish; the draft omits 'Rose-button' translation and the 'romantic name of this aromatic ship' line entirely, losing the chapter's signature wordplay.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Rose-button, or Rose-bud' and close with 'the romantic name of this aromatic ship' — the pun is a deliberate authorial signature.

findings.source_passage: it was like turning up old Roman tiles and pottery buried in fat English loam. His boat's crew were all in high excitement, eagerly helping their chief, and looking as anxious as gold-hunters.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves the Roman tiles simile and gold-hunters comparison but compresses them into a single rushed clause, losing the syntactic pleasure of the original's three-beat construction.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the Roman-tiles comparison its own clause and restore 'eagerly helping their chief' before 'as anxious as gold-hunters' to preserve the rhythm.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful but flattens three voice-establishing passages (the Assyrian-city simile, Stubb's full mock-charity speech, and the 'romantic name of this aromatic ship' pun) at medium severity; no high-severity signature losses were found.
